mainTopic: Does riding (רכוב) on an animal acquire it? The גמרא tests this through several ברייתות: pulling and driving, the rider and the reins, and רבי אליעזר's rider in the field.
overview: This amud asks whether sitting on an animal (רכוב) is a valid way to acquire it. The גמרא first tries to prove from a ברייתא that only pulling (משיכה) and driving (הנהגה) acquire, but each proof is pushed off by explaining how the תנא קמא differs from רבי יהודה. Next, a ברייתא about one person riding a donkey and another holding the reins seems to prove that riding acquires. The גמרא answers that the rider was driving with his feet, and then rereads the ברייתא several times to work out who gets the reins. רב אשי gives a final reading in which each person gets only what he is truly connected to. רבי אבהו's attempt to keep the original wording is rejected as an error. A ברייתא of רבי אליעזר, where riding in the field acquires, is also explained as driving with the feet. Finally, רב אשי shows that an unusual act still acquires, so the ruling that riding in the city does not acquire is limited to a sale where the seller asked for the normal way of acquiring.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא and רבי יהודה's view
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends: the two people acquire in this manner. רבי יהודה disagrees: one acquires only by pulling a camel or driving a donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: They acquired it in this manner. רבי יהודה says: one never acquires unless it is pulling for a camel and driving for a donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא. This sets up the proof about riding that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא lets two people acquire an animal by pulling or driving it. רבי יהודה limits this to the way each animal is normally led: camels are pulled from the front, and donkeys are driven from behind.

keyTerms.meaning: Pulling: leading an animal from the front
Driving: pushing an animal along from behind

phrases.english: In this manner they acquired.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
One never acquires
unless it is pulling for a camel
and driving for a donkey.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לְעוֹלָם לֹא קָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא says pulling or driving acquires. רבי יהודה says it must be pulling a camel or driving a donkey.

steps.title: Inference that riding does not acquire
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists only pulling and driving, so it seems that riding (רכוב) does not acquire.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any event, it teaches: or one was pulling and one was driving. Pulling and driving, yes; riding, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the ברייתא as a proof. Since only pulling and driving are mentioned, it concludes that riding does not acquire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a proof from silence. If riding worked, the ברייתא would presumably have listed it alongside pulling and driving.

keyTerms.meaning: In any event, it teaches (introduces the part of a source being used as proof)

phrases.english: In any event, it teaches:
or where one was pulling
and one was driving.
Pulling and driving: yes.
But riding: no!

steps.triggerLanguage: קָתָנֵי מִיהַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.raayaObject: That riding (רכוב) does not acquire an animal.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא lists only pulling and driving as ways to acquire.

steps.title: Riding may work too; the list is aimed at רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Riding may acquire as well. The ברייתא mentions pulling and driving only to teach, against רבי יהודה, that even the reverse way works.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same is true even of riding. The ברייתא teaches pulling and driving only to exclude רבי יהודה, who requires pulling for a camel and driving for a donkey. It teaches us that even the reverse also acquires.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It gives another reason why the ברייתא mentioned pulling and driving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא was not listing every way to acquire. It was making a point against רבי יהודה: you can pull a donkey or drive a camel and still acquire. So its silence about riding proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude (to argue against a view)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא's first case pairs each animal with its normal method: pulling a camel, driving a donkey. Its second case, 'one pulling and one driving', names no animal. The גמרא reads that second case to mean both methods work for both animals.

phrases.english: The same is true even of riding.
And the reason it teaches pulling and driving
is to exclude the view of Rabbi Yehuda, who says:
only when it is pulling for a camel
and driving for a donkey.
It teaches us that even the reverse
phrases.notes: The reverse means pulling a donkey or driving a camel.

phrases.english: also acquires.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא הַדִּין דַּאֲפִילּוּ רָכוּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference from step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the ברייתא excludes riding.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא mentions pulling and driving for a different reason: to reject רבי יהודה's view. It was not giving a full list of ways to acquire.

steps.title: Then the ברייתא should have combined the cases
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא's point were that both methods work for both animals, it should have said so in one combined sentence.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let it combine them and teach: two who were pulling and driving, whether a camel or a donkey!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the pushback from step 3. The ברייתא's wording does not fit that reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of one combined sentence, the ברייתא pairs pulling with a camel and driving with a donkey. That suggests the תנא קמא partly agrees with רבי יהודה about each animal's normal way, which weakens step 3's reading.

phrases.english: If so,
let it combine them and teach them:
two who were pulling and driving,
whether a camel or a donkey!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, לִיעָרְבִינְהוּ וְלִתְנִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the דחיה of step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 3 that the ברייתא's whole point is that the reverse way also works.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that were the point, the ברייתא would have combined both animals and both methods into one sentence. Its separate pairings suggest it does not fully reject רבי יהודה.

steps.title: One reversed method does not acquire
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא could not combine the cases, because even the תנא קמא holds that one of the reversed methods fails. It is unclear which one.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is one method that does not acquire. Some say it is pulling a donkey, and some say it is driving a camel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 4: why the ברייתא did not just say 'both methods work for both animals.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is that the methods do not all work. Even the תנא קמא agrees with רבי יהודה about one reversed method, so a single combined sentence would have been wrong. There are two opinions on which method that is: משיכה of a donkey or הנהגה of a camel.

keyTerms.meaning: a side, a way or method

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the תנא קמא completely agrees with רבי יהודה. He agrees on only ONE of the two reversed methods. רבי יהודה rejects both.

phrases.english: There is one method by which one does not acquire:
some say: pulling a donkey,
and some say: driving a camel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא חַד צַד דְּלָא קָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the claim: not every reversed method works, so the ברייתא could not combine them.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's point was that both methods work for both animals, so it should have said so in one sentence.
steps.terutzMaskana: One reversed method fails even for the תנא קמא, so the cases had to be written separately.

steps.title: Second version: 'in this manner' excludes riding
steps.stepSummary: In another version, the proof that riding does not acquire comes from the end of the ברייתא: 'in this manner he acquires.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Some raise an objection from the end clause: 'In this manner he acquires.' What does 'in this manner' exclude? Doesn't it exclude riding?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of the discussion. Here the proof against riding comes from the words 'in this manner'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'in this manner' sound like a limit: only these methods work. The most natural thing to leave out would be רכוב, which the ברייתא never mentions. So riding seems not to acquire.

keyTerms.meaning: the end clause of a teaching
in this manner, in this way

phrases.english: And there are those who raise an objection from the end clause:
"In this manner he acquires."
phrases.notes: These are the closing words of the ברייתא from Step 1.

phrases.english: "In this manner" comes to exclude what?
Is it not to exclude riding?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִית דְּמוֹתֵיב מִסֵּיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restarts the discussion in a different version, using a different line of the ברייתא than Step 2.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The limiting words 'בְּמִדָּה זוֹ קָנָה' at the end of the ברייתא.

steps.title: 'In this manner' excludes the reverse
steps.stepSummary: The words 'in this manner' exclude the reversed methods, not riding.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it excludes the reverse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof from Step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'In this manner' means pulling the camel and driving the donkey, as the ברייתא described. It leaves out the reverse: driving a camel or pulling a donkey. Riding is not what is being excluded.

phrases.english: No, it is to exclude the reverse.
phrases.notes: The reverse means driving a camel or pulling a donkey.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, לְמַעוֹטֵי אִיפְּכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the reading that 'in this manner' excludes riding.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The words can just as easily exclude the reversed methods.

steps.title: Then the תנא קמא equals רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: If the תנא קמא excludes the reversed methods, he says the same thing as רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, that is the same as רבי יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said one acquires only by pulling a camel or driving a donkey. If the תנא קמא also rules out the reverse, the two opinions look identical, so there would be no real argument.

phrases.english: If so, that is the same as Rabbi Yehuda!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, הַיְינוּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'in this manner' excludes the reversed methods.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading leaves no difference between the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה.

steps.title: They differ on one reversed method
steps.stepSummary: The difference: the תנא קמא excludes only one reversed method, while רבי יהודה excludes both.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them on one method that does not acquire. Some say it is pulling a donkey, and some say it is driving a camel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 8 by showing where the two opinions still differ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'In this manner' excludes only one reversed method for the תנא קמא. רבי יהודה rejects both reversed methods. So the argument is real, even though we are unsure which method the תנא קמא rejects.

keyTerms.meaning: there is a difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, the תנא קמא agrees with רבי יהודה on one reversed method (either pulling a donkey or driving a camel) but not on the other.

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ צַד אֶחָד דְּלֹא קָנָה:
phrases.english: There is a difference between them: one method by which one does not acquire:
some say: pulling a donkey,
and some say: driving a camel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ צַד אֶחָד דְּלֹא קָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a practical difference between the two opinions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא קמא excludes both reversed methods, just like רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא קמא excludes only one reversed method; רבי יהודה excludes both.

steps.title: Proof that riding acquires
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the rider acquires the donkey and the one holding the reins acquires the reins, so riding acquires.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One is riding a donkey and one is holding the reins. This one acquires the donkey and that one acquires the reins. Learn from it: riding acquires!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא to prove that רכוב does acquire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the attempted proofs said riding does not acquire. Here a ברייתא directly says the rider gets the donkey. That looks like clear proof that riding is a valid way to acquire.

keyTerms.meaning: learn from it (the conclusion of the proof)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
one is riding a donkey
and one is holding the reins –
this one acquires the donkey,
and that one acquires the reins.
Learn from it: one who rides acquires!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אֶחָד רָכוּב חֲמוֹר וְאֶחָד תָּפוּס בְּמוֹסֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proofs against riding were rejected, the גמרא now tries to prove the opposite.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא ruling that the rider acquires the donkey and the one holding the reins acquires the reins.

steps.title: The rider was also steering with his feet
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off: the ברייתא may be talking about a rider who also drives the donkey with his feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is talking about a rider who drives the animal with his feet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 10. It says the rider in that ברייתא was not just sitting; he was also steering the donkey with his feet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Driving an animal (מַנְהִיג) is a known way to acquire it. If the rider was also driving, the ברייתא proves nothing about plain riding. So the question of whether riding alone acquires is open again.

keyTerms.meaning: here too (the same answer as before)
driving or leading an animal, a way of acquiring it

phrases.english: Here too,
it is talking about one who drives with his feet.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי בְּמַנְהִיג בְּרַגְלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the rider-and-reins ברייתא that riding alone acquires.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rider may have acquired by driving with his feet, not by riding.

steps.title: Then the rider should get part of the reins too
steps.stepSummary: If the rider is really driving, he should acquire some of the reins as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the rider should also acquire the reins!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 11. If the rider is fully acquiring by driving, why does the ברייתא give the reins only to the other person?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives the rider only the donkey and gives all the reins to the holder. That suggests the rider's hold is weak, which fits plain riding better than driving. A rider who was driving should also get some of the reins, since they are attached to the donkey.

phrases.english: If so,
the rider should also acquire part of the reins!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, נִקְנֵי נָמֵי רָכוּב בְּמוֹסֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the rider in the ברייתא was driving with his feet.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A driving rider would acquire some of the reins, but the ברייתא gives them all to the holder.

steps.title: Read it as the rider getting half the reins
steps.stepSummary: Change the wording: the rider gets the donkey and half the reins, and the holder gets the other half.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: This one acquires the donkey and half the reins, and that one acquires half the reins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 12 by changing how we read the ברייתא. The rider does get part of the reins: half of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, the ברייתא fits a rider who is driving. He gets the donkey plus half the reins, and the holder gets only the other half.

keyTerms.meaning: say (read the text this way instead)

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא: זֶה קָנָה חֲמוֹר וַחֲצִי מוֹסֵירָה,
phrases.english: Say: this one acquires the donkey and half the reins,
and that one acquires half the reins.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: זֶה קָנָה חֲמוֹר וַחֲצִי מוֹסֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא gives all the reins to the holder, so the rider must not be driving.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rider gets the donkey and half the reins, which fits a driving rider.

steps.title: How does the holder acquire his half?
steps.stepSummary: The rider's half makes sense, but the holder has no clear way to acquire his half of the reins.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, the rider acquires, because a thinking person lifted the reins for him. But how does the one holding the reins acquire?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 13. It accepts how the rider gets his half but asks how the holder gets anything at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rider acquires his half because the holder, a person with understanding, lifted the reins on his behalf. But the reins are tied to the donkey, and the holder does not acquire the donkey. So how can he acquire half the reins?

keyTerms.meaning: a person with understanding, able to have intent

phrases.english: Granted, the rider acquires,
because a thinking person lifts it for him.
phrases.notes: The 'thinking person' is the one holding the reins, and his lifting counts for the rider.

phrases.english: But the one holding the reins, by what means does he acquire?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא רָכוּב קָנֵי, דְּקָמַגְבַּהּ לֵיהּ בֶּן דַּעַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the new reading given in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the holder acquires half the reins.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reins are attached to the donkey, which the holder does not acquire, so he has no way to acquire half the reins.

steps.title: The holder gets only what is in his hand
steps.stepSummary: Change the wording again: the rider gets the donkey and the reins, and the holder gets only the part in his hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: This one acquires the donkey and all the reins, and that one acquires what he holds in his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 14 with a new reading. The holder only gets the piece of rein actually in his hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rider gets the donkey and the rest of the reins, still because the holder's lifting counts for him (the reason from step 14). The holder gets only the part he is gripping, which he acquires by lifting it directly. The next step attacks the idea that the holder's lifting can count for the rider.

keyTerms.meaning: what he is holding in his hand

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא: זֶה קָנָה חֲמוֹר וְכוּלֵּיהּ מוֹסֵירָה,
phrases.english: Say: this one acquires the donkey and all the reins,
and that one acquires what he holds in his hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: זֶה קָנָה חֲמוֹר וְכוּלֵּיהּ מוֹסֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A second rereading of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The holder acquires a full half of the reins, with no clear way to do so.
steps.terutzMaskana: The holder acquires only the part in his hand; the rider gets the rest.

steps.title: The holder lifted the reins for himself, not for the rider
steps.stepSummary: The rider cannot acquire through the holder's lifting, because the holder meant to take the reins for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this? Even if you say that one who lifts a found item for his friend makes his friend acquire, that only applies when he lifts it with his friend in mind. This man lifts it with himself in mind. If he does not acquire it, can he make others acquire it?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks how the rider was said to acquire the reins (step 14): through the holder's lifting. That cannot work, because the holder was lifting for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lifting for someone else can work only if you mean to acquire for that person. Here the holder wanted the reins for himself, and he did not acquire them. If his lifting does not work for him, it cannot work for the rider either. רב אשי answers this in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: what is this? (how can that be?)
even if you will say (even if we accept this)
one who lifts a found item for his friend

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying the holder made the rider acquire on purpose. The point is the opposite: the holder only wanted the reins for himself, so his lifting cannot count for the rider.

phrases.english: What is this?!
Even if you will say
that one who lifts a found item for his friend, his friend acquires,
that applies only where
he lifts it with his friend in mind.

phrases.aramaic: הַאי אַדַּעְתָּא דִּידֵיהּ קָא מַגְבַּהּ לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: This one lifts it with himself in mind:
he himself does not acquire, so can he make others acquire?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי מַאי?! אִם תִּימְצֵי לוֹמַר הַמַּגְבִּיהַּ מְצִיאָה לַחֲבֵירוֹ קָנָה חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the reason given in step 14 for the rider acquiring the reins and attacks it, which also undercuts the reading in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the rider acquires the reins because the holder lifted them for him.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Lifting for another works only when done with the other person in mind. Here the holder lifted for himself and did not acquire, so his lifting cannot count for the rider.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a key limit: lifting can count for someone else only when the person lifting means it for them.

steps.title: Rider gets the donkey and head-strap, the holder gets only what is in his hand
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rereads the ברייתא so that each person acquires only what he is truly connected to. The middle part of the reins goes to no one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The rider acquires the donkey and the strap on its head. The holder acquires only the part of the reins in his hand. The rest of the reins is acquired by neither of them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the problem from step 16 by changing the wording of the ברייתא one more time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rider no longer needs the holder's lifting. He gets only the donkey and the strap tied to its head, which go along with the animal itself. The holder gets just the piece he is gripping, and the loose part in between stays ownerless.

keyTerms.meaning: the halter, the part of the reins attached to the donkey's head

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
This one acquires the donkey and its halter,
and that one acquires what is held in his hand,
and the rest was not acquired
by neither this one nor that one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב אשי זה קנה חמור ובית פגיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16 by removing the rider's need for the holder's lifting.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording the ברייתא (a new reading of the text)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rider would need the holder's lifting to acquire the reins.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rider acquires only the donkey and the head-strap. The holder acquires only what he holds, and the middle stays ownerless.

steps.title: Keep the original wording: the holder can pull the reins to himself
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says there is no need to change the ברייתא. The holder acquires the reins because he can pull them free and bring them to himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: Really, the ברייתא means exactly what it says. The holder acquires the reins, since he can pull them off and bring them to himself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו offers a different approach: leave the ברייתא as written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the original wording, the rider gets the donkey and the holder gets the reins. רבי אבהו explains that the holder acquires all the reins without lifting them, because he is able to detach them and pull them over to himself.

keyTerms.meaning: really, it is as it is taught (no change to the text)

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
Actually, it is as it is taught,
since he is able to detach it
and bring it to himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי אבהו אמר לעולם כדקתני
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from רב אשי's, without rewording the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New legal reasoning that keeps the original text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא had to be reworded because the holder had no way to acquire the reins.
steps.terutzMaskana: The holder acquires the reins because he can detach them and draw them to himself.

steps.title: רבי אבהו's reasoning is a mistake, as the garment case shows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא calls רבי אבהו's idea an error. Using it would wrongly give a garment lifted by two people to only one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו's view is a mistake. If not, take a garment lying half on the ground and half on a pillar. One person lifts the half on the ground and another lifts the half on the pillar. Would we also say the first acquires it and the second does not, since he could pull it all to himself? Clearly not. So רבי אבהו's view is a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רבי אבהו by showing his rule leads to a wrong result in another case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being able to pull something to yourself were enough, then in the garment case the first lifter would get the whole garment. Everyone agrees that is not the law. So 'he could pull it over' is not a real way to acquire, and רבי אבהו's answer falls. The question of whether a rider acquires stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: the first one / the later one

phrases.english: And this statement of Rabbi Abbahu is an error,
for if you do not say so:
a garment that is lying
half of it on the ground
and half of it on a pillar,

phrases.aramaic: וּבָא אֶחָד וְהִגְבִּיהַּ חֶצְיָהּ מֵעַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע
phrases.english: and one came and lifted half of it off the ground,

phrases.aramaic: וּבָא אַחֵר וְהִגְבִּיהַּ חֶצְיָהּ מֵעַל גַּבֵּי עַמּוּד,
phrases.english: and another came and lifted half of it off the pillar,
would we also say that the first one acquires
and the later one does not acquire,
since he is able to detach it
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets are added in the corrected wording, making the word mean 'it'.

phrases.english: and bring it to himself?!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הָא דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ בְּרוּתָא הִיא.
phrases.english: Rather, this statement of Rabbi Abbahu is an error.

steps.triggerLanguage: והא דרבי אבהו ברותא היא דאי לא תימא הכי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Throws out רבי אבהו's alternative answer from step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי אבהו's whole reasoning that being able to pull an item to yourself acquires it.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would give the garment only to the first lifter, which is plainly wrong.
steps.whatToRemember: Being able to pull something over to yourself does not acquire it. רבי אבהו's approach is rejected, and the question about a rider is still open.

steps.title: Attempted proof from רבי אליעזר that riding acquires
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי אליעזר says someone riding in the field acquires the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי אליעזר says, one who rides in the field or leads in the city acquires.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new proof that riding on an animal is a valid way to acquire it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר lists רכוב, riding, as a way to acquire in the field. That seems to prove that sitting on the animal acquires it, which would answer the open question.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Rabbi Eliezer says:
one riding in the field
or leading in the city acquires!

steps.triggerLanguage: תא שמע רבי אליעזר אומר רכוב בשדה ומנהיג בעיר קנה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי אבהו is rejected, the גמרא tries a fresh source for the open question.
steps.raayaObject: That riding on an animal acquires it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי אליעזר: רכוב בשדה קנה.

steps.title: The rider here is driving the animal with his feet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes the proof aside. רבי אליעזר's rider is actually driving the animal with his feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it means he is leading the animal with his feet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by reading רבי אליעזר's case differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rider in רבי אליעזר's case may be kicking or pushing the animal forward with his feet. That is a form of driving, not plain sitting. So the case does not prove that just sitting on the animal acquires it.

phrases.english: Here too, he is leading it with his feet.

steps.triggerLanguage: הכא נמי מנהיג ברגליו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from רבי אליעזר's case of riding.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rider may be driving with his feet, so the case is not about plain sitting.

steps.title: Then riding is the same as leading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if the rider is driving, that is the same as מנהיג, so why list it separately?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, that is the same as leading!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading from step 21.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר names two cases, riding and leading. If riding just means driving with the feet, it seems to be the same case as leading. Then the ברייתא would be repeating itself.

phrases.english: If so, that is the same as leading!

steps.triggerLanguage: אי הכי היינו מנהיג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading given in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי אליעזר's rider is driving with his feet.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That would make 'riding' and 'leading' one case, so the ברייתא would say the same thing twice.

steps.title: There are two kinds of leading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא lists two different types of מנהיג.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are two kinds of leading.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection and keeps the reading from step 21.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One kind is driving from on the animal, using the feet. The other is driving from on foot, as in the city. The ברייתא lists both, so there is no repetition. רבי אליעזר's case therefore still does not prove that plain sitting acquires.

phrases.english: There are two kinds of leading.

steps.triggerLanguage: תרי גווני מנהיג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting one term into two separate cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Riding with the feet and leading are one and the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are two different kinds of leading, so the proof from riding falls and the question stays open.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר's 'rider' can be read as someone driving with his feet. So his ברייתא does not prove that just sitting on an animal acquires it.

steps.title: Why doesn't riding in the city acquire?
steps.stepSummary: If a rider acquires because he drives the animal with his feet, a rider in the city should acquire too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the reason that one who sits on an animal in the city does not acquire it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own new explanation. If the rider in the field acquires because he drives the animal with his feet, a rider in the city does the same thing, so he should acquire too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 said the rider acquires because he is driving with his feet, which is a kind of מנהיג. A rider in the city also drives with his feet. So the ruling that a rider in the city does not acquire now needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: introduces a problem that follows from what was just said
Someone sitting on an animal in the city

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: He means: if riding acquires because the rider drives the animal with his feet, as the גמרא just said.

phrases.english: one who sits on an animal in the city
what is the reason he does not acquire?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, רָכוּב בָּעִיר מַאי טַעְמָא לָא קָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation from steps 21-23 that the rider acquires by driving with his feet.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that riding acquires because the rider drives the animal with his feet
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rider in the city also drives with his feet, so the ruling that he does not acquire seems to contradict this idea.

steps.title: People don't usually ride in the city
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא explains that riding in the city is not the normal way, so it does not acquire.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: Because people do not normally ride in the city.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers the question. Riding in the city does not acquire because it is not how people normally act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer adds a new requirement: an act of acquiring works only if it is the normal way people do things. In a crowded city, people do not usually ride, so riding there does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not the normal way of people

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין דַּרְכָּן שֶׁל בְּנֵי אָדָם
phrases.english: Because it is not the way of people
to ride in the city.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין דַּרְכָּן שֶׁל בְּנֵי אָדָם לִרְכּוֹב בָּעִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a condition: an act of acquiring must be the normal way people act
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Driving with the feet should acquire everywhere, even in the city
steps.terutzMaskana: Riding in the city is not normal, so it does not acquire

steps.title: Lifting a purse on שבת still acquires
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי shows that an unusual action, like lifting a purse on שבת, still acquires. So riding in the city should acquire too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to רב כהנא: If that is so, if someone lifted a purse on שבת, since people do not normally lift a purse on שבת, would he also not acquire it? Rather, what he did, he did, and he acquires it. Here too, what he did, he did, and he acquires.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks רב כהנא's answer with a comparison. Someone who lifts a found purse on שבת surely acquires it, even though people do not normally do that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'not the normal way' blocked acquiring, then lifting a purse on שבת would not acquire, and that is clearly wrong. Since an action that was actually done counts even if it is unusual, riding in the city should acquire too. So רב כהנא's reason falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: But if that is so: introduces a result that seems wrong
What he did, he did: the act counts even if it was unusual

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying lifting a purse on שבת is allowed. He is saying that once someone did it, the act still works to acquire the purse.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב כָּהֲנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Rav Kahana:
But if that is so,
if one lifted a purse on Shabbat,
since it is not the way of people
to lift a purse on Shabbat,
would he also not acquire it?
Rather, what he did, he did, and he acquires;

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי מַאי דַּעֲבַד – עֲבַד, וּקְנִי.
phrases.english: here too, what he did, he did, and he acquires.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב כָּהֲנָא: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב כהנא's answer from step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's rule that an unusual action cannot acquire
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Lifting a purse on שבת is unusual but clearly acquires. So being unusual does not stop an act from acquiring, and riding in the city should acquire too.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about buying and selling
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא speaks about a sale where the seller said, 'Acquire it the way people normally acquire.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we are dealing with buying and selling, where the seller said to him: Acquire it the way people normally acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to why riding in the city does not acquire. The ברייתא is about a sale, and the seller set a condition: acquire it only the normal way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In general an unusual act does acquire, as רב אשי proved. But a seller can limit how the buyer may acquire. Since he said 'the way people normally acquire,' and people do not ride in the city, riding there does not work in this sale.
steps.whatToRemember: An unusual act still acquires (מאי דעבד עבד). Riding in the city fails only in a sale where the seller said to acquire in the normal way.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule from רב אשי stands: an act that was done counts even if unusual. The limit in the ברייתא comes from the seller's own words, not from a general rule.

phrases.english: Rather, we are dealing with buying and selling,
where he said to him:
phrases.notes: The seller is speaking to the buyer.

phrases.english: Acquire the way that people acquire.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּמִקָּח וּמִמְכָּר עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב כהנא's answer, which step 26 knocked down, with a new reading of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: a sale with a condition from the seller
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Riding in the city fails because unusual acts never acquire
steps.terutzMaskana: Unusual acts do acquire. Here riding in the city fails only because the seller required the normal way of acquiring.
